gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Noto Sans Mahajani stands tall, lowercase nearly level with its capitals. Noto Sans Mahajani keeps a funnel-wide e that lets paragraphs flow easily under Nippo, whose strokes bend like paperclip wire.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-mono: Nippo draws small letters that stand nearly capital-tall, each stroke looking cut from thin wire with no lighter parts. Nippo catches attention, while Noto Sans Mono keeps its sturdy letters generously apart.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-multani: Technical in spirit, Nippo has strokes that look cut out by a router bit, its small letters nearly capital-sized. And Noto Sans Multani sits lofty and open beside it, its wide-gapped e softening the sharp edges.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Wire-cut and uniform, Nippo keeps its bars identical in thickness from the first letter to the last. Noto Sans Nabataean does the quieter work, with lowercase rising almost cap-tall and wide-open s curves.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-old-italic: Thin, steady and technical, Nippo draws its small, nearly capital-sized letters with variation in stroke absent. Noto Sans Old Italic, with little gap between x-height and cap height, does well at modest sizes under a bigger Nippo.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-old-permic: Wire-cut letters, small yet nearly capital-sized, give Nippo a pen pressure that never changes from first to last. Noto Sans Old Permic stays approachable line after line, rounded and open.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Clean in feel, Nippo sketches small, nearly capital-sized letters as if a pencil never pressed harder. Noto Sans Sundanese joins in with open e crossbars, tying the two together.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Noto Sans Sunuwar is clean and approachable, with curves that leave daylight. With rounded-wire strokes, Nippo loses its punch if made small, so give it room while the body stays modest.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Noto Sans Telugu reads smoothly, its high midline keeping counters open. Nippo does the showing off with its technical pipe-cleaner strokes, leaving the quieter work to the text beneath.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Wire-cut and technical, Nippo joins its strokes at full width instead of thin hairlines. And Noto Sans Ugaritic brings the approachable part, its open mouths like chalk arcs left unjoined.
